examples.en: The rice ripened and the grains turned yellow.
Sparrows pick up and eat grains in the paddy.
Grandfather begrudged even a single fallen grain.
The grains ripened firmly in the sunshine.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹을 때 낟알 하나까지 남기지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: When I eat, I try not to leave even a single grain.
I picked out only the grains and put them in a sack.

explain: 곡식의 알 하나하나를 말해요. '이삭'은 알이 달린 줄기 부분이고, '낟알'은 거기서 나온 알이에요. 소리 나는 대로 [나달], '낟알이'는 [나다리]로 읽어요.
explain_en: It means the individual kernels of grain. '이삭' is the ear of the plant where grains grow, and '낟알' is the grains themselves. It is read [나달], and '낟알이' is read [나다리].

examples.en: At the fishing spot, my father caught a big fish.

examples.ko: 이번에 잡은 대어는 길이가 한 팔이나 됐어요.
examples.en: The big fish I caught this time was as long as an arm.

examples.ko: 물속에 대어가 숨어 있는지 한참을 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited a long time to see if a big fish was hiding in the water.

examples.ko: 대어 한 마리 때문에 하루 종일 낚시터에 있었어요.
examples.en: I stayed at the fishing spot all day for the sake of one big fish.
Unfortunately, I lost the battle with the big fish.
He is a player called the big catch of the scouting market.

explain: 큰 물고기를 말하는데, 비유로는 영입하고 싶은 유명한 사람이나 따내고 싶은 큰 계약을 가리켜요. 스포츠 영입, 수주, 인수 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 비슷한 말은 '월척'인데, 이것은 낚시에서 큰 물고기를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 올해 최고 선수를 영입해 대어를 낚았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 성과를 거두거나 중요한 인물·계약을 얻었을 때 써요. 낚시 이야기가 아니라 비유로 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you achieve a big result or win an important person or contract. It is a figurative expression, not about fishing.

explain_en: It literally means a big fish, and figuratively a famous person someone wants to sign or a major deal someone wants to win. You see it in news about player signings, contract wins, and acquisitions. A similar word is '월척', which is used for a big fish in fishing.

examples.en: On the summer night, we lit a mosquito fire in the yard.
The smoke from the mosquito fire made my eyes sting.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁에서는 모깃불이 아직도 익숙한 풍경이에요.
examples.en: At my grandfather's house, a mosquito fire is still a familiar sight.
We ate watermelon next to the mosquito fire.

examples.ko: 아이들이 모깃불 주위에 둘러앉아 옛날이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: The children sat around the mosquito fire and listened to old stories.

examples.ko: 불이 꺼지지 않게 모깃불에 마른 쑥을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: I added more dry mugwort to the mosquito fire so it wouldn't go out.

explain: 모기를 쫓으려고 풀이나 쑥 같은 것을 태워 연기를 내는 불이에요. 요즘은 '모기향'이나 전자 모기향을 쓰니까 시골 이야기나 옛날 추억에서 더 자주 나와요. 보통 '모깃불을 피우다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a fire that burns grass or mugwort to make smoke and drive away mosquitoes. Today people use '모기향' or electric repellents, so the word appears more often in countryside stories and old memories. It is usually said as '모깃불을 피우다'.

examples.en: A new unmanned shop opened in our neighborhood.
At an unmanned shop, you have to pay by yourself.
Late at night I dropped by a self-service shop and bought ice cream.

examples.ko: 저는 무인점포를 이용하는 게 아직 어색해요.
examples.en: I still feel awkward using unmanned shops.

examples.ko: 무인점포 앞에서 사용 방법을 한참 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read the instructions for a long while in front of the unmanned shop.
The store that was run as an unmanned shop has closed.

explain: 직원 없이 손님이 직접 고르고 계산하는 가게예요. '무인 카페', '무인 세탁소'처럼 '무인'을 붙인 말과 함께 써요. 반대는 '유인 점포'보다 그냥 '일반 가게'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It's a shop where customers choose and pay on their own without staff. It goes with other '무인' words like '무인 카페' and '무인 세탁소'. For the opposite, people simply say '일반 가게' (regular shop).

examples.ko: 주말에는 가족과 함께 별식을 만들어 먹어요.
examples.en: On weekends I make and eat a special dish with my family.
For lunch today I had kalguksu as a change from the usual.

examples.ko: 할머니가 가끔 해 주시는 별식이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The special dishes my grandmother occasionally makes are the tastiest.

examples.ko: 매일 밥만 먹다가 별식이라도 먹으니 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: After eating plain rice every day, even a little treat lifts my mood.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 별식 생각이 나요.
examples.en: On rainy days I start thinking of a special treat to eat.

examples.ko: 별식은 특별한 날이 아니어도 가끔 먹으면 좋아요.
examples.en: A special dish is nice to have once in a while, even on ordinary days.

explain: 평소 먹는 밥과 다르게 가끔 해 먹는 음식을 말해요. '별미'는 특별히 맛이 좋은 음식이라는 느낌이 강하고, '별식'은 늘 먹던 것과 다르다는 데 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to food you eat now and then that differs from your usual meals. '별미' stresses food that tastes especially good, while '별식' focuses on being different from what you always eat.

examples.en: Pork belly tastes greasy if it has too much fat.
I cut the fat off the meat before eating.

examples.ko: 비계 부분이 고소해서 좋아하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people like the fatty part because it is rich and nutty.

examples.ko: 돼지고기 비계에서 기름을 내서 볶음밥에 써요.
examples.en: I render oil from pork fat and use it for fried rice.
Please give me only the lean meat and leave out the fat.
Don't leave just the fat, eat it all.

explain: 주로 돼지고기나 소고기에서 말하고, 반대말은 '살코기'예요. 식당이나 정육점에서 '비계 빼 주세요'처럼 자주 말해요. 건설 현장의 '비계'는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to the fat on pork or beef, and its opposite is '살코기' (lean meat). You often hear '비계 빼 주세요' at restaurants and butcher shops. The '비계' used at construction sites is a different word that only sounds the same.

examples.ko: 도매 시장에서는 소매점보다 훨씬 싼 값에 물건을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: At a wholesale market you can buy goods at a much cheaper price than at retail stores.
This brand is sold at retail stores nationwide.

examples.ko: 동네 소매점이 대형 마트 때문에 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The local retail shop closed because of the big supermarket.

examples.ko: 소매점을 열려면 먼저 위치부터 정해야 해요.
examples.en: To open a retail store, you first have to decide the location.
Prices differ a little from one retail store to another.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 도매도 하고 소매점도 같이 해요.
examples.en: Our business does wholesale and runs a retail store as well.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '가게'나 '상점'이라고 하고, '소매점'은 도매와 비교하거나 유통 이야기를 할 때 써요. 소비자에게 직접 파는 곳이라는 점이 도매 시장과 다른 점이에요.
explain_en: In daily life people simply say '가게' or '상점', and '소매점' is used when contrasting with wholesale or talking about distribution. What sets it apart from a wholesale market is that it sells directly to consumers.

examples.ko: 불법 어선의 싹쓸이 조업이 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: Sweep-net fishing by illegal boats is becoming a problem.
It was the day our class swept all the prizes.

examples.ko: 이번 대회는 한국 선수들의 싹쓸이로 끝났어요.
examples.en: This tournament ended with a clean sweep by the Korean players.

examples.ko: 휴가 전에 마트에서 싹쓸이 쇼핑을 했어요.
examples.en: Before the vacation, I did a grab-everything shopping spree at the mart.
That drama swept the awards at the ceremony.

examples.ko: 숲을 싹쓸이 벌목하면 산사태 위험이 커져요.
examples.en: If a forest is clear-cut, the risk of landslides grows.

explain: 상, 메달, 물건을 한꺼번에 다 가져가는 것을 말하고, 어업이나 벌목에서는 하나도 남기지 않고 다 가져가는 나쁜 방식을 가리켜요. 보통 '싹쓸이하다'나 '싹쓸이로'처럼 써요. 구어로는 '싹 쓸어 가다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means taking everything at once, such as prizes, medals or goods, and in fishing or logging it refers to the bad practice of taking everything without leaving anything. It is usually used as '싹쓸이하다' or '싹쓸이로'. In casual speech people also say '싹 쓸어 가다'.

examples.ko: 율무차를 마시면 속이 편해지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like my stomach settles when I drink adlay tea.

examples.ko: 쌀에 율무를 조금 섞어서 밥을 지었어요.
examples.en: I mixed a little adlay into the rice and cooked it.

examples.ko: 율무는 고소해서 죽으로 끓여 먹어도 맛있어요.
examples.en: Adlay is nutty, so it's also good boiled into porridge.
I bought a bag of adlay at the market.

examples.ko: 할머니가 율무를 볶아서 차로 끓여 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother roasted adlay and brewed it into tea for me.

examples.ko: 율무가 들어간 과자는 처음 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: This is my first time eating a snack with adlay in it.

explain: 쌀이나 보리처럼 곡식의 한 종류예요. 밥에 섞거나 죽을 끓이고, 볶아서 '율무차'로 마시는 방법이 흔해요.
explain_en: It is a kind of grain like rice or barley. It is commonly mixed into rice, cooked as porridge, or roasted and drunk as '율무차' (adlay tea).

examples.en: The neighborhood bookstore is closing down next month.
Customers decreased, so we decided to close the shop.
Many restaurants closed down during COVID.
I heard the news that the owner is closing down.
After closing the business, I looked for new work.
If you close a business, you must report it to the tax office.

explain: 폐업하다는 가게나 회사가 영업을 완전히 끝낼 때 써요. 잠깐 쉬는 '휴업하다'와 달라서 다시 열지 않는다는 느낌이에요. 문을 열고 새로 시작하는 건 '개업하다'예요.
explain_en: 폐업하다 is used when a shop or company ends its business completely. It differs from 휴업하다, which means closing for a while, because 폐업하다 feels like it will not reopen. Starting a business is 개업하다.

examples.en: The ship met a storm and drifted at sea.
A small boat has been drifting for several days.

examples.ko: 그 사업이 계속 표류할 것 같아 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried that project will keep drifting without direction.
I feel like I'm drifting without a goal.

examples.ko: 구명조끼를 입은 사람이 사흘간 표류하다 구조됐어요.
examples.en: A person wearing a life jacket drifted for three days and was rescued.
If the negotiations drift, the schedule keeps getting pushed back.

explain: 원래는 배가 바다에서 정해진 길 없이 떠다니는 것이고, 비유로 계획·협상·인생이 방향을 잃고 흔들릴 때도 써요. 같은 '떠다니다'는 물건이 가볍게 떠 있을 때도 쓰지만, '표류하다'는 어려운 상황이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Originally it means a ship drifting at sea without a set course, and figuratively it covers plans, negotiations or a life that has lost direction. '떠다니다' can describe anything floating lightly, but '표류하다' carries the feeling of being in a difficult situation.

examples.en: The wind direction changed today, so the fine dust decreased.

examples.ko: 풍향과 풍속을 알아야 바람을 정확히 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You need to know both wind direction and speed to understand the wind precisely.

examples.ko: 산불은 풍향에 따라 번지는 방향이 달라져요.
examples.en: The direction a wildfire spreads changes depending on the wind direction.
The weather agency observes and announces the wind direction.

examples.ko: 요트 선수는 풍향을 살피며 배를 움직였어요.
examples.en: The sailor checked the wind direction while moving the boat.
The wind direction shifted from the northwest to the southeast.

explain: 풍향은 바람이 불어오는 쪽을 말해서 '북풍'은 북쪽에서 불어오는 바람이에요. 바람의 빠르기는 '풍속'이라고 해서 날씨 이야기에서는 풍향과 풍속을 짝으로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 풍향 is the direction the wind comes from, so '북풍' is a wind blowing from the north. How fast the wind blows is '풍속', and the two are often mentioned as a pair in weather talk.
